 Taylor Ardrey USA TODAY Oct. 28, 2026, 10:40 a.m. ET Hear this story Your car's exterior lighting may be defective.
 FCA US LLC is recalling more than 13,000 vehicles because the tail lights aren't illuminating properly, according to a notice posted by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.
 "The terminals in the tail light wiring harness may be damaged and cause the tail lights to fail," the notice says.
 Here's what we know about the recall and what drivers should do next.
 Car recalls: Ford recalls over 30K trucks. See the affected models Which model is affected?
 According to the NHTSA, 13,330 vehicles were potentially affected. The model included is:
 2026 Dodge Durango
 The recall number is A2D. The issue could impact visibility for the motorist and others on the road, increasing the risk of a crash.

See affected models Volvo recalls more than 9,000 vehicles. See affected models Ford recalls more than 102K vehicles. See the affected models What should car owners do?
 Car owners are urged to take their vehicle to a dealership to have the tail light assemblies replaced at no cost.
 Notification letters will be sent out on Dec. 4.
 Chrysler can be reached at 800-853-1403.
 Taylor Ardrey is a news reporter for USA TODAY. You can reach her at tardrey@usatodayco.com.
